title: MADGER - The Cost of Control
scope: Six sources of pressure within the existing factions; thirteen character addenda; seven reusable locations; a season-one evidence and escalation ledger; two complete antagonist stories.
status_rule: Operating histories, location aliases and fixed normal-state details are additive writer canon. Character choices, scene seeds and complete stories are authored options until adopted by a dated episode ledger. No pilot villain reveal is added.
moral: A good act does not buy ownership of another person. Protection earns trust when people can question it, refuse it and help shape it.

base_factions.name: Burrow Commons
base_factions.purpose: Keep a welcoming town livable, fair and defensible. This names the civic cooperation already present in the Bible; it does not replace ward decisions with a new ruler.
base_factions.leadership: Ward delegates, open meetings and rotating work coordinators. Madger convenes and serves; his founder status gives him no permanent veto. Snow is a protected companion, not an office-holder.
base_factions.methods: Shared stores, maintenance rosters, public explanations, rescue practice and accountable protective closures. Disputes concern priorities and evidence, not whether ordinary residents deserve safety.
base_factions.tension: Welcome versus capacity. Pell wants understandable procedures; Iona wants verified limits; Madger sometimes promises both before consulting either.
base_factions.ties: Commonworks supplies expertise; the Wayfarer Accord brings visitors and goods. The Commons opposes coercion by the Gilt Ledger, intrusion by Glass Thread and predation by Riven Claw.

base_factions.name: Commonworks Fellowship
base_factions.home: Stonewake and a regional workshop network
base_factions.purpose: Make essential knowledge teachable so no settlement depends on one indispensable specialist.
base_factions.leadership: Oren Vale coordinates exchanges. Iona is the Burrow contact; Tavi is an apprentice participant, never an unsupervised emergency specialist.
base_factions.methods: Travelling repair crews, apprenticeships, shared specifications and tool loans. Each town keeps local authority over its own machinery.
base_factions.tension: Their careful standards can postpone urgent improvisation. Oren must learn when a temporary repair is responsible, while Madger must accept when it is unsafe.
base_factions.ties: Works with the Commons and Wayfarers. Refuses exclusive maintenance deals from the Gilt Ledger. Glass Thread can steal records, but cannot acquire practical mastery by downloading them.

base_factions.name: Wayfarer Accord
base_factions.home: Latchford; independent crews across the road network
base_factions.purpose: Keep travel, rescue and honest exchange possible for people without powerful sponsors.
base_factions.leadership: Sela Venn coordinates convoy safety. Lark Quill carries dispatches and keeps route accounts. Crews can decline a route they cannot safely serve.
base_factions.methods: Guides, escorted caravans, weather reports and voluntary rescue agreements. Their wagons are finite; an invitation does not create transport capacity.
base_factions.tension: Keeping a promised timetable may conflict with stopping for strangers. Sela supports Madger but will not endorse a comforting promise she cannot fulfill.
base_factions.ties: Supplies the Burrow and transports Commonworks crews. Pays legitimate tolls, contests Gilt Ledger coercion, and resists Riven Claw raids. Lark occasionally buys information from Pip Skein.

base_factions.name: Gilt Ledger
base_factions.home: Privately controlled warehouses and offices in Reedbank
base_factions.purpose: Make independent settlements reliant on its depots, credit and permission to trade. Its public promise is dependable supply; its private objective is lasting leverage.
base_factions.leadership: Director Veyra Kest sets policy. Corvin Silt brokers contracts and influence. Bale Nacre controls stock, transport allocations and collections.
base_factions.methods: Exclusive supply terms, selective shortages, pressure on indebted operators and purchased information. It owns particular businesses, not Reedbank or every merchant.
base_factions.tension: Veyra calls dependence stability. Corvin profits from ambiguity; Bale knows that a frightened workforce eventually stops cooperating.
base_factions.ties: Buys limited information jobs from Glass Thread through Corvin. It has no command over the hacker crew. It sometimes buys stolen goods through intermediaries but regards Riven Claw as an expensive disruption.

base_factions.name: Glass Thread
base_factions.purpose: Sell privileged information and turn uncertain records into influence. Members claim that exposing weak systems excuses exploiting the people who rely on them.
base_factions.leadership: Nix Vey chooses targets and negotiates jobs. Tessera Keen handles social access and forged identities. Patch Serein maintains stolen equipment and relays.
base_factions.methods: Fictional record tampering, impersonation and constrained system intrusions. Access requires a particular opportunity; local controls, human checks and physical barriers still matter.
base_factions.tension: Nix wants recognition; Tessera wants profitable anonymity; Patch wants an exit before someone is physically harmed. Remorse does not erase responsibility.
base_factions.ties: Accepts selected Gilt Ledger contracts and keeps its own secrets. Distrusts Riven Claw, whose violence destroys useful contacts. Writer-only v1.1 answer: Tessera’s limited relay probe causes D17. Madger does not know Glass Thread’s membership at the pilot; Snow’s scent is unrelated.

base_factions.name: Riven Claw
base_factions.home: Disused freight terraces in the Cinder Cuts
base_factions.purpose: Extract supplies and obedience from travellers and weaker outposts. Its leader treats possession as something proved through force.
base_factions.leadership: Brakka Mourn commands raids. Dreg Husk controls hauling and shares. Vessa Rake scouts routes and bargains for intelligence.
base_factions.methods: Ambush, intimidation and theft of movable supplies. They need food, rest, transport and local knowledge; they cannot appear anywhere without a route.
base_factions.tension: Brakka prizes spectacle, Dreg wants sustainable provisions, and Vessa resents being treated as expendable. Their cooperation depends on rewards and fear.
base_factions.ties: Sells through fences including Pip, who can refuse a deal. It has occasional transactions with Gilt Ledger intermediaries, no standing alliance. No species is inherently loyal to this band.

base_factions.name: Free Harbors Compact
base_factions.home: A treaty among Crownrest, Ossara public wells, Nacre Quay, Aurel Quay and Lumen Tide; no capital
base_factions.purpose: Protect passage, rescue rights and local ownership of knowledge without turning mutual aid into annexation.
base_factions.leadership: Rotating local delegates; any new obligation requires the affected community’s consent.
base_factions.methods: Reciprocal refuge, shared weather observations and narrowly scoped archive exchanges.
base_factions.tension: Secrecy protects some communities but can endanger visiting travelers. Wealthier ports try to dominate timetables.
base_factions.ties: Works with Wayfarers and Commonworks. Opposes water coercion, sky ransom and extraction without agreement.

base_factions.name: Blackwake Sails
base_factions.home: A mobile fleet using an abandoned mooring outside Aurel Quay
base_factions.purpose: Turn emergency passage into permanent tribute.
base_factions.leadership: Serik commands three small cargo craft; captains bargain over shares and can desert.
base_factions.methods: False promises, seized cargo and ransom; real rescue skill makes the deception credible.
base_factions.tension: Crew members want profit and survival, not Serik’s theater of heroism.
base_factions.ties: Occasional trade with Riven Claw; no global villain command structure. Eri knows their procedures.

base_factions.name: Still Bell Archive
base_factions.alignment: Divided institution / protective and authoritarian wings
base_factions.purpose: Preserve Severance evidence and assess dangerous resonant crossings.
base_factions.leadership: Ossa controls the senior council; Ysolde leads a disclosure faction.
base_factions.methods: Technical records, measured closure orders and field inspections. Ossa additionally forged a modern prohibition.
base_factions.tension: Real expertise can become a monopoly on judgment. Most archivists are neither villains nor infallible sages.
base_factions.ties: Needs independent Hollow Sea records; disputed by Free Harbors; Commonworks can test physical claims.

pressure_centers.title: Gilt Ledger: the price of certainty
pressure_centers.promise: You will never have to wonder whether the next wagon is coming.
pressure_centers.history: Veyra built her influence by solving real supply problems. During the flood seven years before the pilot, she paid for the second rescue convoy without a public bargain. That choice saved people. In the years afterward, she acquired depot contracts and began treating successful provision as evidence that communities should surrender future choice. Her later coercion does not retroactively make the rescue a staged crime.
pressure_centers.routine: Bale opens with a physical stock count. Corvin arrives later with amendments that turn ordinary purchases into longer obligations. Workers load legitimate orders beside selectively withheld freight. Some admire Veyra because she pays consistently; others have families waiting outside her terms. The depot should feel attractive and competent before the cost of that competence becomes visible.
pressure_centers.internal_conflict: Veyra wants a defensible system. Corvin needs private exceptions that make him indispensable. Bale needs a workable loading floor. A side commission can enrich Corvin while making both the policy and the stock count harder to defend. They cooperate because each supplies something the others lack, not because they share one conscience.
pressure_centers.limits: The Ledger owns particular stock and businesses. It does not own Reedbank, the public kitchen, the Burrow gates, every road or every merchant. Glass Thread can refuse its jobs. Riven Claw can raid its freight. A supply promise remains limited by wagons, labor and weather.
pressure_centers.story_turn: When the rescue invoice becomes public, the apparent twist is that Veyra truly helped. The deeper conflict is whether gratitude can be converted into consent. Let her make one costly good choice in the present while retaining an unacceptable demand elsewhere.
pressure_centers.hero_test: Madger must acknowledge the rescue honestly and still let residents reject the monopoly. Pell makes the terms understandable; Iona tests whether the promised supply can actually be delivered.

pressure_centers.title: Glass Thread: the right fact in the wrong hands
pressure_centers.promise: If they will not record us, we will make their records impossible to ignore.
pressure_centers.history: Nix returned from teenage work seasons with Madger to a Millmere restoration process that overlooked some households. Their grievance is genuine. Later paid access work gave them equipment, contacts and a dangerous audience. Tessera joined for profitable anonymity, and Patch followed maintenance pay. Their shared origin story is convenient: each remembers a different moment when the work stopped being defensible.
pressure_centers.routine: They lease rooms briefly, pay for ordinary meals, mend equipment and argue over what a client actually purchased. Tessera separates identities; Nix keeps recognizable scraps of old route language; Patch labels components because a wrong part still breaks a machine. The crew has no universal view of the world. An unattended message is as likely to remain unread as anyone else’s.
pressure_centers.internal_conflict: Nix wants the public to know who forced the truth into view. Tessera wants nobody to connect a useful identity to a crime. Patch wants a future workshop whose tools are not evidence. Each can expose the other two, but doing so would also expose their own choices.
pressure_centers.limits: D17 is a bounded receipt replay through a compromised trade relay. No code, credentials or real intrusion procedure is specified. Corrupted messages do not open a physical latch. Glass Thread needs a particular access opportunity and can lose it through ordinary witnesses and source comparison.
pressure_centers.story_turn: A surviving document proves that an omitted community really existed, while a different document proves that Nix endangered travelers. Both stay true. The heroes cannot dismiss the grievance because its messenger committed a crime, or excuse the crime because the grievance is true.
pressure_centers.hero_test: Bot must admit what a record cannot establish. Madger must rescue strangers before pursuing an old friend. Snow follows ordinary scent and behavior; she cannot identify a hacker or detect guilt.

pressure_centers.title: Riven Claw: the cost of spectacle
pressure_centers.promise: Nobody will leave us hungry or treat us as disposable again.
pressure_centers.history: The Cinder freight diversion eighteen years before the pilot caused real hardship. Brakka, once a convoy guard, founded her band seven years ago. Those dates are distinct: she did not invent the decline and has no mandate from the people harmed by it. The occupied civilian terraces remain a community of workers and families, most of whom want the raiders gone.
pressure_centers.routine: Dreg sorts freight, checks harnesses and apportions meals. Vessa reports routes she has actually observed. Brakka stages arrivals and punishments as theater. A ledger of shares keeps the band together as much as fear does. Rest, damaged wheels and insufficient water can postpone a raid; animals and workers cannot march indefinitely for a dramatic cut.
pressure_centers.internal_conflict: Brakka wants obedience visible from a distance. Dreg wants usable provisions. Vessa wants her knowledge respected and an escape from expendability. Burning supplies can therefore satisfy the leader while destroying the bargain that keeps her specialists working.
pressure_centers.limits: The band travels by known routes. Vessa’s flight has weather and load limits. It cannot appear inside the Burrow or bypass inner defensive closure. Ashmouth is separate from civilian Cinder Cuts. Trade with Serik or a Ledger intermediary creates a transaction, not a chain of command.
pressure_centers.story_turn: Dreg’s record of victims first looks like conscience. It began as insurance for himself. What changes him is not discovering a hidden tender nature, but choosing to use a useful bargaining asset for restitution and accepting what that costs.
pressure_centers.hero_test: Gorilla must protect a retreat instead of accepting a public challenge. Madger must work within the town’s assigned roles. Edda treats injured people without confusing treatment with exemption from responsibility.

pressure_centers.title: Salt Crown: scarcity made proprietary
pressure_centers.promise: One coordinated water account is fairer than a thousand arguments at the wells.
pressure_centers.history: Kavar acquired pump interests through successive dry seasons. His certificates began as convenient records of delivered water and became instruments of dependence. He is a commercial counterpart within the Ledger network, not a new global faction or Veyra’s puppet. Ossara’s three public wells predate his business by centuries.
pressure_centers.routine: Public-facing clerks weigh claims, inspect containers and explain legitimate maintenance costs. Kavar surrounds the process with handsome objects and precise language. The lie sits in a specific maintenance account and a competing pump kept closed, not in the existence of arithmetic or every clerk’s intentions.
pressure_centers.internal_conflict: Local staff need their wages and reliable water for their own homes. Some believe closure protects an exhausted aquifer. Kavar benefits from their caution while withholding the evidence that would let them distinguish a real limit from a manufactured one.
pressure_centers.limits: Exposing a false debt does not refill the aquifer. Pumps still need parts, trained maintainers and water-budget decisions. The counting house has records and instruments, not a hidden control that governs every well in the desert.
pressure_centers.story_turn: The first exposed invoice is genuinely wrong, but a second shortage is real. A cheap victory would accuse every warning of being a lie. A strong episode makes Maela defend a measured restriction moments after helping expose Kavar’s fabricated one.
pressure_centers.hero_test: The heroes must accept local expertise. Madger cannot promise limitless water; Commonworks can help restore equipment only under a community-agreed allocation.

pressure_centers.title: Blackwake Sails: rescue with a ransom attached
pressure_centers.promise: When everyone else turns back, we are the ones who come for you.
pressure_centers.history: Serik was a capable rescue captain before he began turning emergency passage into ransom. Expulsion did not erase his skill. He now commands three small cargo craft and uses an abandoned mooring outside Aurel Quay. Former clients remember real rescues, making testimony against him emotionally difficult without making it unreliable.
pressure_centers.routine: Crews mend sails, calculate loads and argue about shares. Serik rehearses the arrival he wants survivors to remember. His people know that a generous-looking rescue can become a debt at the next berth. Some remain for money, others because leaving requires a safe port and a captain willing to hire them.
pressure_centers.internal_conflict: Serik needs admiration; captains need craft that can return. A spectacular pursuit can cost a vessel and turn supporters into witnesses. Eri’s knowledge of ordinary load rules is more useful than discovering a mystical weakness.
pressure_centers.limits: Three craft remain three craft. He cannot make storms, control the liftstone field or command every sky crew. Heavy cargo, wind and counterweights constrain him. The mooring has three docking arms and two refuge cells, not an unbounded fleet base.
pressure_centers.story_turn: He saves a crew member during the escape because he has real rescue instincts. The same survivor can later testify that he held others for ransom. A good act complicates the portrait; it does not cancel the charge.
pressure_centers.hero_test: Local navigators lead. Gorilla protects loading space, Bot checks stated load data and Madger helps free people without promising an impossible airlift.

pressure_centers.title: Still Bell: authority after the emergency
pressure_centers.promise: We remember what happens when a confident person reconnects the wrong thing.
pressure_centers.history: The Severance occurred ninety-two years before the pilot. Ossa did not cause it. She inherited accounts of a real protective sacrifice and later forged one modern prohibition to retain control over decisions. Most archivists preserve useful knowledge; the institution contains both protective work and authoritarian choices.
pressure_centers.routine: Archive staff compare copies, inspect material and send field teams when weather allows. Genuine hazard reports share shelves with Ossa’s altered order. Ysolde’s disclosure work requires painstaking comparison, not an eloquent accusation followed by instant certainty.
pressure_centers.internal_conflict: Ossa fears that admitting one forgery will make people ignore every warning. Ysolde fears that secrecy will eventually make every warning unbelievable. Ysolde must publish her own family’s benefit from prolonged closure rather than placing herself outside the history she reveals.
pressure_centers.limits: The Cut Span retains a real gap and resonance hazard. The forged modern order and the justified old closure are separate claims. Exposing the first does not make the second safe. Echo ice stores fragments, not omniscient testimony or resurrected witnesses.
pressure_centers.story_turn: The dramatic victory is a shared process that can test both claims, preserving one closure while withdrawing another. Ossa loses exclusive judgment, not the usefulness of everything she learned.
pressure_centers.hero_test: Bot keeps uncertainty visible; Commonworks tests physical claims. Madger learns to live with a partial reopening that serves people without pretending the whole ancient network is safe.

character_addenda.name: Veyra Kest

baseline.name: Veyra Kest
baseline.seed: Ledger director and hidden funder of the second flood convoy. Demands dependency in return for security; runs with Corvin and Bale.
baseline.design: Female sable, deep chocolate fur, ivory chin, ink-blue tailored long coat, one warm brass clasp, composed posture.
baseline.history: Reedbank depot worker who rose through crisis logistics. At thirty-eight she diverted reserves to fund a rescue convoy; later consolidation convinced her that only centralized control prevents chaos.
baseline.desire: To make the Burrow sign a permanent exclusive supply agreement and prove that her form of order is indispensable.
baseline.contradiction: Her generosity becomes a claim of ownership. She remembers every life she helped but discounts lives injured by her conditions.
baseline.relationships: Corvin negotiates; Bale controls stock; Sela knows the rescue truth; Kavar is an occasional commercial counterpart.
baseline.arc: Season one: her offer fails despite a genuine good deed. Later: she must choose between saving her ledger and releasing stock without a binding promise. An act of repair can cost her power without erasing accountability.
baseline.story_engine: A negotiation where her diagnosis is partly right; a crisis in her own depot that exposes how little her workers trust her.
baseline.writer_truth: She did not cause the flood, invent Nix’s grievance or command Brakka’s raid. Her culpability is her present coercion.

character_addenda.private_history: As a young depot worker, Veyra once stayed after closing to match an unclaimed parcel to the family whose name had been copied incorrectly. She remembers the correction as proof that a reliable system needs someone willing to take charge.
character_addenda.ordinary_habit: Straightens the unused chair before a negotiation, even when she expects the other person to refuse it.
character_addenda.pressure_point: A public subscription solves a supply problem she sincerely believed required her contract.
character_addenda.irreversible_choice: Releases a finite emergency allotment before anyone signs her preferred agreement.
character_addenda.cost_of_change: She loses a real bargaining advantage. Workers and residents may acknowledge the release while still opposing the monopoly.
character_addenda.scene_seed: Madger thanks her in public. She waits for the second sentence that will turn thanks into consent. It does not come.

locations.history: After freight was diverted, this loading terrace lost its regular traffic. It retains a refuge lodge and service approaches because those were useful before Brakka arrived. The band’s occupation turns a workplace into a coercive store without making its original builders or the neighboring population complicit.
locations.daily_life: Dreg keeps crates sorted by use and remembers which harness needs repair. The west approach admits wagons; the east route is a narrow foot path. A fenced gas trough stays outside the working court. Ashmaws follow heat plumes in the wider terrain; neither Brakka nor Dreg commands them.
locations.dramatic_use: The loading platform makes a public order visible. When Brakka demands spectacle and Dreg protects usable supplies, everyone on the floor sees the split. Escape follows the registered approaches; the shelter offers cover and rest, not a hidden passage to town.

locations.name: Blackwake Mooring
locations.ownership: Abandoned mooring occupied by Serik’s three-craft crew.
locations.history: The platform was built for regulated cargo transfer within a local liftstone field. Its counterweights and load rules are older than Serik’s claim to the place. His occupation gives him a berth and a stage; it does not give him ownership of the air routes or control over the field.
locations.daily_life: One main winch deck feeds three docking arms. The rear refuge lodge uses the existing two shelter bays as separate refuge cells. A short connector links it to the deck. Each craft has a finite load envelope and must be counted in the scene state: berthed, arriving or away. Three small craft cannot become an unseen reserve fleet.
locations.dramatic_use: Eri recognizes a routine loading limit that Serik is trying to conceal. The heroes free people by making a viable departure possible, not by cutting every support and hoping the platform floats anyway. Captives and cargo compete for capacity; useful evidence may have to be left behind.

locations.name: The Cut Span
locations.ownership: A genuinely closed crossing inspected by Still Bell and independent reviewers.
locations.history: The deliberate severing belongs to the historical response to the Severance. Ossa’s later forged prohibition is a separate act. The north and south inspection places allow evidence to be gathered without reopening the gap. The longer foot detour still takes two days and leaves this sheet.
locations.daily_life: Inspectors approach their own abutment, compare marks and stop at the guarded edge. Detached couplings are examined behind the north rail. The north refuge remains at its inherited position; a measured south inspection lodge completes the two-house description already established in the atlas.
locations.dramatic_use: Expose a false order beside a dangerous structure that deserves a truthful warning. A refusal to reconnect can be the responsible outcome even when the official who demanded it has lied. No visual hint should turn the gap into an easy leap for the heroes.

The generic v3.0 encounter polyline is a staging guide, not permission to walk across the severed span. This edition resolves safe north and south approach paths separately and retains the 20 m blocked gap. The two-day detour leaves the sheet; no short bypass is added.

Existing site footprints, regional coordinates and refuge footprints remain fixed. New features fill previously schematic encounter fields. The 3.2 detailed collision and approach layers control local staging within those fixed bounds.

Ashmaws respond to heat plumes and choirwraiths occupy the dangerous ridge beyond inspection limits. They are environmental beings with established behavior, not faction-controlled weapons or a reason to label a whole species evil.

Public welcome and inner protective closure remain distinct. No secret bypass, magical master machine or unregistered tunnel is introduced. Snow remains quadrupedal and non-speaking; approved hero likenesses and voices continue to control production.
